chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, both together from Ibn Mahboub from Abu Wallad from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

There is no mutual compensation (by blood relatives) among the People of the Covenant regarding what they incur of killing or injury; rather, that is taken from their wealth. So if they do not have wealth, the crime liability returns to the Imam of the Muslims, because they pay the Jizya to him, just as the slave pays the tribute to his master.
He (peace be upon him) said: And they are the slaves of the Imam, so whoever from them becomes Muslim, he is free.

key_terms.أَهْلِ الذِّمَّةِ: People of the Covenant (non-Muslims under protection)

ai.seo_question: Who pays the blood money for crimes committed by non-Muslims under Muslim rule?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* clarifies that the *Ahl al-Zimma* are exempt from the customary tribal blood-guild (*mu'aqala*) paid by their kin, as their political subordination to the Imam makes them akin to slaves (*mamaliik*). Consequently, the Imam assumes financial liability for their crimes if they lack personal wealth, a ruling derived from their payment of the *jizya*. This establishes a distinct legal status where conversion to Islam immediately grants them full freedom and removes this specific liability structure.
